what: The two hard tasks left from the approved re-run, on the build with the reasoning-effort fix, Rune against OpenCode, both gpt-6-sol on Codex.
authorisedBy: the founder, 2026-10-08: re-run the three hard tasks, six agent runs, stop at 70%. Two runs were used on the first task (b2-s5); these are the other four.

build.rune: a clean clone at 81a321e, run from source

rune.verdict: partial: three criteria it stated, one satisfied, two needing review

whatItShowed.the_cache: On both tasks Rune's second request was served from the cache (11,776 and 11,648 cached tokens) and no later request lost it. The day before, the second request read 0 on all three tasks.
whatItShowed.a_failure_that_predates_the_run: On model-catalog-cache the suite was red on the same two tests as the day before. This time the check said `preexisting`, the notice named both tests as already failing, no repair was asked for, and the project's package.json was not touched. The run made 15 calls for $0.25 where it had made 23 for $0.45, and it cost less than OpenCode's ($0.34).
whatItShowed.what_the_check_still_costs: On model-catalog-cache the end of the run took 85 s: the check, then the same check on the tree the run started from, which is what it takes to know the failures were not the run's. On startup-selection the suite was waited for once, 120 s, and measured nothing, as on any first run in a fresh workspace; the touched test file was then run and passes.
whatItShowed.the_bill: Three tasks, one run each: Rune $2.21 and 1,379 s, OpenCode $1.76 and 908 s (the first task on the build before the effort fix). The day before: $2.14 and 1,382 s against $2.03 and 1,153 s. OpenCode was faster on all three than the day before; Rune's own working time went from 890 s to 1,042 s. Neither tool's call counts repeat from one day to the next: Rune 27 then 39 on one task, OpenCode 40 then 28 on the same one.
whatItShowed.the_reviewer: $0.38 of Rune's $2.21 across the three tasks: screens and reviews on gpt-6-astra.
whatItShowed.the_verdict: Rune called all three finished runs unfinished again: 'partial' twice, 'unmet: no criteria stated' once.

limitations: One run a task. The swing between two days is larger than any effect these changes could have on time or total cost; only what each change does mechanically is shown.
No score: two builds across the three pairs, and three pairs is half of what a score needs.
With the effort fix, ordinary turns on Codex reason at the ceiling. Whether that makes the work better, or only dearer, is not measured.
The Codex CLI's own use of the same subscription cannot be seen from here. Rune's meter read 61% at the end.
